response.passage: The Sentinel of the Bay, an old lighthouse built in 1892, stands tall on the rocky coast of Ratnagiri. For decades, Captain Vikram guided ships safely past the jagged reefs using the lighthouse’s powerful rotating beam. The structure was constructed with thick granite blocks to withstand the fierce monsoon gales that batter the coast every year. Because the salt spray from the Arabian Sea constantly corrodes the iron railings, the local caretaker, Mr. D’Souza, spends 15 hours every month painting them to prevent rust. Visitors often mistake the lighthouse for a fort because of its sturdy, circular walls. However, the building was never designed for defense. Its primary purpose was to provide a steady light for sailors navigating the dark, treacherous waters at night. Today, the lighthouse remains a silent witness to the changing tides, reminding everyone of the days when manual navigation was the only way to survive the sea.
response.summary: The Sentinel of the Bay is a historic lighthouse in Ratnagiri built in 1892. It was designed to guide ships safely through dangerous waters rather than for military defense.
